question.problem: An arithmetic series has the first term ${a}_{1}=2$, the $6$th term ${a}_{6}=22$, and the sum of the series is ${S}_{N}=288.$ Find the number of terms $N$ in the series.
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series.

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d)
$$

Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{6}-{a}_{1}}{6-1} \\  & =\frac{22-2}{5} \\  & =\frac{20}{5} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting ${a}_{1}=2$, $d=4$, and ${S}_{N}=288$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 288 & =\frac{N}{2}(2\cdot 2+(N-1)\cdot 4) \\ 288 & =\frac{N}{2}(4+4N-4) \\ 288 & =\frac{N}{2}(4N) \\ 288 & =2{N}^{2} \\ 144 & ={N}^{2} \\ N & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we take the positive square root because $N$ can't be negative.
